plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through snow and frost, making it one of the earliest signs of the end of winter in temperate Europe and in gardens elsewhere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Europe and Southwest Asia; widely naturalized in woodlands and gardens in the UK, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a natural antifreeze-like protein, and the compound galantamine, first isolated from related plants, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that bears fragrant flowers on bare branches in the coldest part of winter. Its blossoms are prized in East Asian art, poetry and gardens as symbols of perseverance and hope.
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated across Japan, Korea, China and in gardens worldwide, including warm temperate regions of the US
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms bloom before cherry blossoms, and in Japan their appearance signals the approach of spring, with ume festivals held in February.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A large deciduous shrub with spidery, ribbon-like, strongly scented flowers that appear on leafless branches in winter. The flowers curl up in freezing weather to protect themselves and unfurl again when it warms.
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens in Europe, North America and Japan
plants.funFact: Witch hazel flowers can survive being frozen, as their petals roll up tightly in the cold and then reopen when temperatures rise.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Proteaceae family, up to 30 cm across, made of a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by showy pink bracts. It thrives in the fynbos vegetation of South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Flowers mainly in late winter to spring in South Africa, with sporadic blooms in summer; the Southern Hemisphere summer to autumn period can also see flowers
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its ancient lineage dates back more than 300 million years, with a genus name taken from the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape.
